title: Preventive Maintenance and Breakdown Management of Equipme
html:
Preventive Maintenance and Breakdown Management of Equipment

A. PURPOSE

To ensure:

  • Safe and reliable functioning of all medical and non-medical equipment
  • Reduction of equipment downtime
  • Timely preventive maintenance and effective breakdown management
  • Compliance with NABH and regulatory requirements

B. SCOPE

Applies to:

  • All medical equipment
  • Non-medical equipment
  • All hospital departments

C. POLICY STATEMENT

The hospital ensures that:

  • All equipment is maintained through a structured preventive maintenance program
  • Equipment breakdowns are addressed promptly and efficiently
  • Maintenance activities are documented and monitored
  • Only trained and authorized personnel handle equipment maintenance

D. DEFINITIONS

  • Preventive Maintenance (PM): Scheduled servicing to prevent equipment failure
  • Breakdown Maintenance: Repair carried out after equipment failure
  • Calibration: Process of verifying accuracy of equipment
  • AMC/CMC: Annual/Comprehensive Maintenance Contract

E. RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Administrator

  • Prepare maintenance schedules
  • Ensure timely servicing and calibration
  • Maintain records and documentation
  • Coordinate with vendors

2. Department Heads

  • Ensure proper usage of equipment
  • Report breakdowns immediately

3. Users (Doctors/Nurses/Technicians)

  • Handle equipment properly
  • Perform basic checks before use
  • Report faults promptly

4. Director

  • Approve AMC/CMC contracts
  • Allocate budget for maintenance

F. PROCEDURE

1. EQUIPMENT INVENTORY MANAGEMENT

  • Maintain updated inventory of all equipment including:
    • Name, model, serial number
    • Location
    • Supplier/vendor details
    • Warranty/AMC status
  • Assign unique identification number to each equipment

2. PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE PLAN

2.1 Scheduling

  • Prepare annual PM schedule based on:
    • Manufacturer recommendations
    • Usage frequency
    • Criticality of equipment

2.2 Frequency

  • Daily / Weekly checks (user level)
  • Monthly / Quarterly / Half-yearly / Annual maintenance

2.3 Activities

  • Cleaning and inspection
  • Functional testing
  • Calibration
  • Replacement of worn-out parts
  • Safety checks

2.4 Execution

  • Conducted by:
    • Biomedical team OR
    • Authorized vendor (AMC/CMC)

2.5 Documentation

  • Record:
    • Date of maintenance
    • Work performed
    • Parts replaced
    • Next due date
  • Maintain PM checklist for each equipment

3. CALIBRATION

  • Perform calibration for critical equipment:
    • Monitors, ventilators, lab equipment, etc.
  • Maintain calibration certificates
  • Ensure traceability to standards

4. BREAKDOWN MAINTENANCE PLAN

4.1 Reporting of Breakdown

  • User must:
    • Stop using faulty equipment immediately
    • Inform Biomedical Department
    • Tag equipment as “Out of Order”

4.2 Logging

  • Record in breakdown register/software:
    • Equipment ID
    • Location
    • Nature of fault
    • Date and time

4.3 Response Time

  • Define turnaround time (TAT):
    • Critical equipment: Immediate / within 1–2 hours
    • Non-critical: Within 24 hours

4.4 Repair Process

  • Initial inspection by biomedical team
  • Minor repairs done in-house
  • Major repairs referred to vendor

4.5 Standby Arrangement

  • Provide backup equipment for critical areas
  • Ensure continuity of patient care

4.6 Post-Repair Validation

  • Test equipment before reuse
  • Ensure safety and functionality
  • Remove “Out of Order” tag

4.7 Closure

  • Update breakdown log with:
    • Action taken
    • Downtime
    • Responsible person

5. AMC/CMC MANAGEMENT

  • Maintain valid AMC/CMC contracts
  • Track service visits and compliance
  • Evaluate vendor performance

6. SAFETY MEASURES

  • Electrical safety checks
  • Use of proper grounding
  • Avoid overloading
  • Follow manufacturer guidelines
